title: CascadeCloud x Redwood partner intro
summary: Introductory partner discovery between Redwood and CascadeCloud to explore a reseller / cloud integration partnership. High-level goals: marketplace listing + joint go-to-market, technical integration options (direct VPC peering, marketplace AMI, managed offering), benchmark/pilot for TCO and latency, compliance alignment (SOC2, KMS). Agreed next steps: exchange partner deck and security pack, schedule technical deep-dive with infra/ops, scope a 4-week pilot and joint benchmark plan.

transcript:
Header: Date: 2026-07-27 | Time: 15:00 PDT | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood), Priya Sharma (Redwood SE), Samir Gupta (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (CascadeCloud), Vikram Patel (CTO), Angela Cho (Cloud Architect), Leo Martins (Product)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect): quick intro, partner goals, technical clarifications about VPC and private deployments, GPU types, pilot scope, regulatory/compliance check, next steps.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. I'm Jordan Lee, AE on partnerships at Redwood, and with me are Priya and Samir from our solutions team. Um, really excited to learn about CascadeCloud and see how we can partner.

[00:18] Marta: Hi! Thanks Jordan. I'm Marta, head of partnerships at CascadeCloud. We run a marketplace and managed cloud offering, and we're looking at adding inference-first LLM offerings. A quick note, some of our customers ask for pre-bundled GPU stacks and managed service options.

[00:35] Priya: Awesome. Can you tell us, like, is the ask more about a marketplace image/AMI, or a managed integration where Cascade runs Redwood Dedicated under the hood? Or both?

[00:48] Vikram: Good question. Short term we want a marketplace listing (AMI + onboarding flow) so customers can spin up quickly. Mid-term we want to evaluate a managed option where we host reserved capacity for joint customers; that would need more ops integration and shared SLOs.

[01:10] Samir: Got it. A couple clarifying Qs  what GPU types do you expose today and what's your typical region coverage? Also curious about networking patterns: do you prefer VPC peering, Transit Gateway, or private link-ish models?

[01:28] Angela: We have A100 80G and some H100 machines in us-west-2 and eu-west-1 today; we spin up other hardware on demand. Network-wise we've been doing VPC peering and private link for security-sensitive customers. We can support Transit Gateway too.

[01:45] Jordan: That maps well to Redwood  we support hosted API, dedicated reserved pools, and private deployments (VPC/on-prem). For managed/reseller models, typically vendors start with a marketplace image and then we do a pilot on dedicated reserved capacity to validate perf and economics.

[02:03] Marta: Sounds reasonable. On the business side, what's your typical revenue split or partner program terms? We can go into specifics later but high level expectations help.

[02:14] Jordan: We'll send our partner one-pager and pricing grid. High level, we have referral and reseller models; for managed, we can do committed capacity with shared pricing outlines. I'll get that over after this call.

[02:28] Vikram: Great. On technical, Priya, can you walk through what you need to run a benchmark/pilot? Our infra folks will want concrete steps.

[02:36] Priya: Sure. Typical pilot: 1) Define target models and sequence lengths (e.g., 2-4 model variants, Llama-2-type or MPT, up to 2k tokens). 2) Choose instance types (A100/H100), quantization profiles if used (we support int8 or nf4). 3) Provide sample traces or synthetic loads. 4) Run joint benchmark comparing latency p95, throughput, and cost per token. We'll also test KV cache/prefix caching behaviors.

[03:10] Angela: About quantization  do you require specific kernels? We sometimes see issues with certain quantized runtimes.

[03:18] Samir: We have kernel selection in our runtime but there are corner cases; for pilot we usually try a few quantization profiles and measure quality regressions. Note: transcription here might show 'kernels' as 'carnels' cause nm, haha.

[03:34] Marta: For enterprise customers we need to show compliance  SOC2, encryption in transit and at rest, KMS/HSM support, audit logs. How does Redwood handle this for private deployments?

[03:45] Priya: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS, HSM integrations, SSO/SAML for RBAC, and audit logs shipped to your SIEM. We have SOC2 Type II cert; we'll share a security pack. There may be a short legal questionnaire for the marketplace listing too.

[04:05] Vikram: Good. Latency targets  many of our customers in fintech want sub-150ms p95 for short prompts. Is that realistic?

[04:13] Samir: Depends on model, sequence length, and batching. For smaller context it's often achievable on local GPU, but if you're routing to hosted APIs across regions there is network overhead. For dedicated pools in the same region, sub-150ms for short prompts is possible with the right model and configuration. We'll include network and VM placement in the benchmark.

[04:42] Jordan: On go-to-market, do you have a partner onboarding flow and marketplace technical requirements? Also, what's your ICP  self-serve startups vs enterprise?

[04:55] Marta: Our ICP is mid-market to enterprise  they want managed offerings and marketplace procurement. We have a standard marketplace checklist: AMI/Container image, onboarding docs, security questionnaire, pricing metadata, and optionally a managed SaaS listing.

[05:10] Priya: Perfect. For integration options, we can support: 1) Marketplace AMI/Container + quickstart; 2) Private deployment template for customers in Cascade VPC with VPC peering; 3) Dedicated reserved capacity where Cascade runs a Redwood Dedicated pool for customers. Each has different operational burden.

[05:30] Angela: For option 2 (private), what's the deployment pattern? Do you provide terraform modules or helm charts?

[05:38] Samir: We have terraform templates and helm charts for private installs. For VPC deployments we do an initial onboarding script and then an ops handover. We'll attach pre-reads.

[05:48] Marta: On joint marketing, we can do a launch blog, marketplace spotlight, and co-hosted webinar. If the pilot shows strong TCO wins vs competitors (Equinox, Aurora), we can prioritize go-to-market.

[06:05] Jordan: Love that. One more question: do you have enterprise customers that require data residency in EU? We can support region pinning and private deployments for that.

[06:15] Vikram: Yes, several. We'll want EU region options and notes on where logs are stored.

[06:23] Priya: We'll include region coverage and logging practices in the security pack.

[06:30] Marta: Timing  if we aim to have a pilot by early August, what's reasonable?

[06:36] Jordan: If we get the pre-reads this week (workloads and SLOs), Priya and Samir can scope a pilot and we'll aim for a 4-week engagement starting ~2026-08-10. That aligns with your dates.

[06:48] Vikram: Sounds good. What about pricing for pilot  any estimate?

[06:52] Jordan: We'll provide a sample pricing/discount grid for partners. Pilots are often subsidized or discounted depending on committed usage. We'll detail in the partner one-pager.

[07:05] Angela: A quick technical sidebar  do you support GPU sharing/multi-tenant on same instance? We run multiple smaller workloads and sometimes want fractional GPU.

[07:15] Samir: Redwood's runtime supports multi-tenant scheduling and fractional allocation through our batching primitives, but it's workload dependent. For strict isolation, dedicated GPU per tenant is recommended. We'll test both in the benchmark.

[07:33] Marta: Ok let's recap next steps.

[07:36] Jordan: Recap: Jordan to share partner deck + pricing grid and security pack by 2026-07-30; Priya to schedule a technical deep-dive with Vikram/Angela for week of 2026-08-03; Cascade to send sample workloads and go-to-market ICP by 2026-08-05; Agree pilot SOW and success metrics by 2026-08-10. We'll also include a joint benchmark plan to test A100 vs H100, quant profiles, and latency/cost numbers.

[08:05] Marta: Yup that's it. Thanks everyone. We'll look for the deck and security docs.

[08:12] Jordan: Thanks all  talk soon.

Notes: transcription has occasional mis-hears (e.g., 'KV cash' instead of 'KV cache', 'Redweed' occasionally). References to artifacts: Redwood partner deck (link to be shared), security pack (link to SOC2 and KMS docs), benchmark spreadsheet (will be shared).
